artworks.title: Oedipus at Colonus
artworks.description: Harriet's Colonus — the blind exile led by Antigone into Attic sacred ground, Sophocles' last Theban play as revolutionary-era pathos.

artworks.title: Oedipus and Antigone
artworks.description: Brodowski's father and guide — Oedipus and Antigone on the road that ends at Colonus, dependence remade as piety.

artworks.title: The Blind Oedipus Commending his Children to the Gods
artworks.description: Gagneraux's blind king entrusting his children to the gods — the aftermath that Colonus will turn into Athens' hidden blessing.

artworks.title: Ismene and Antigone Plead with Theseus
artworks.description: Abildgaard's Ismene and Antigone before Theseus — the Attic king who receives the Labdacid exile as Sophocles wrote him.

popCulture.title: Oedipus at Colonus
popCulture.creator: Sophocles
popCulture.description: Sophocles' last Theban play — the blind exile received by Theseus, dying as Athens' hidden protector among the Eumenides.

popCulture.title: Oedipus
popCulture.description: The cursed king who ends as a blessing — Colonus turns the Labdacid exile into Attic foundation myth.
